summary.headline: Q1 FY27 total income INR411 crores, EBITDA INR79.3 crores at 19.3% margin, PAT INR37.5 crores; Dombivli drag INR9.5 crores.
summary.overview: Q1 FY27 was the first full quarter of operations for Dombivli Hospital, which contributed a INR9.5 crore EBITDA drag, in line with management's expectations. Consolidated total income was INR411 crores, EBITDA INR79.3 crores (19.3% margin) and PAT INR37.5 crores. ARPOB rose to INR73,500 and ALOS was 3.76 days, with average occupancy at 59.6% diluted by the expanded Dombivli bed base. Management kept Dombivli's guidance (EBITDA loss of INR2-3 crores per month on operating beds, breakeven in roughly 1.5-2 years) unchanged and confirmed the Indore expansion and a backward-integration IV fluids acquisition.

financial_highlights.value: approx. zero; roughly INR500 crores debt and INR500 crores cash (approximate, per management)

segments.name: Thane
segments.commentary: Occupancy stuck at mid-70s (about 75%); growth expected to track inflationary pricing with limited occupancy upside.

segments.name: Pune
segments.commentary: Occupancy in low-to-mid 60s; management expects growth to plateau or slow in percentage terms as the remaining ~15% occupancy headroom is filled, with pricing as a further driver.

segments.name: Indore
segments.commentary: Occupancy about 50%; revenue up about 10% YoY but EBITDA margin about 12% on new team buildup and doctor hires (a couple of crores of added cost). Expected to grow faster than Thane and Pune as occupancy improves.

segments.name: Dombivli
segments.commentary: First full quarter; occupancy roughly 25-30%; operating on about 200 beds with a further ~300 beds upcoming; fixed cost about INR6-7 crores per month; EBITDA loss guidance INR2-3 crores per month; oncology (radiation/LINAC) expected by year-end.

guidance_outlook: Dombivli EBITDA loss guidance of INR2-3 crores per month on currently operating beds retained; EBITDA breakeven guided at 1.5-2 years, with management saying the second year should be the breakeven year.
ARPOB expected to grow at inflation for mature units and above inflation for new units for a few years as case mix improves.

Ramp-up model: initial EBITDA drag for the first 1-2 years per hospital; after reaching about 60% occupancy on installed beds, capacity is added to bring occupancy back to about 40%, with some margin compression but no EBITDA loss.
Board-imposed debt ceiling of 3x EBITDA; current capex expected to be funded by internal accruals and cash, with debt possibly needed toward the end of the cycle.
Five-year visibility: all three announced projects to be delivered within five years; focus on Western India.
Management declined to give full-year FY27 margin guidance beyond the Dombivli inputs.
capex_capacity: Three upcoming projects on track; line of sight to around 3,000 beds with the growing footprint.
Dombivli operating on about 200 beds, with about 300 more beds to be commissioned.
Indore being readied for the next phase of expansion.
IV fluids manufacturing line acquired as backward integration for the pharmacy subsidiary, costing about INR35-40 crores including infrastructure; management says it is not a shift into pharma.
Management described the BKC hospital as a new site ~100 m from the bullet train station.
demand_pricing: ARPOB growth of about 10% in the quarter, driven by a combination of case-mix improvement and insurance contract renegotiations.
Dombivli payer mix mostly self-paid; insurance empanelment (cashless) still pending and expected to reduce friction and lift occupancy.
Dombivli oncology not fully launched; CGHS empanelment not planned immediately, to be considered later under revised pricing.
Doctor hiring at Dombivli to continue for a couple of years as subspecialties are added; ~30-40 full-time doctors plus visiting doctors at present.

qa_highlights.question: Why did Indore EBITDA margin fall to about 12% despite about 10% revenue growth, and is the 13-14% growth expectation for existing units realistic?
qa_highlights.answer: Higher costs reflect new team buildup and doctor hires for the next expansion phase (a couple of crores). Management does not model unit-by-unit growth but said Thane will grow with inflation, Pune faster on occupancy, and Indore faster still.

qa_highlights.question: Is Dombivli's guidance still valid, and could breakeven come sooner?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the guidance still holds (breakeven in 1.5-2 years); it is not being aggressive until one or two more quarters of data are in.

qa_highlights.question: What is the Dombivli occupancy, fixed cost and doctor count?
qa_highlights.answer: Occupancy about 25-30%; fixed cost about INR6-7 crores per month, expected to rise somewhat over the next 1-2 years; about 30-40 full-time doctors plus visiting doctors.

qa_highlights.question: Why did the company acquire an IV fluids manufacturing unit?
qa_highlights.answer: Backward integration for the pharmacy subsidiary to manage costs and improve margins; capital cost about INR35-40 crores including infrastructure, not a move into pharma.

qa_highlights.question: Why is Pune's growth slowing?
qa_highlights.answer: Pune is at mid-60s occupancy with about 15% headroom left; growth will plateau or slow in percentage terms, unlike earlier phases.

qa_highlights.question: What is the debt and cash position and pledged-share issue?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the pledge is by a non-promoter party, unchanged, with the increase in share count due to the split reported erroneously as a 5x pledge increase. Net debt is about zero, with roughly INR500 crores of debt and INR500 crores of cash (approximate).

risks_watch: Dombivli ramp-up: occupancy at 25-30% against an EBITDA loss of INR2-3 crores per month and fixed costs of INR6-7 crores per month; watch whether occupancy improves after insurance empanelment.
Thane and Pune occupancy plateauing near mid-70s and mid-60s, limiting volume growth to pricing.
Indore margin compression from expansion hiring ahead of occupancy gains (currently about 50%).
Rising fixed costs as Dombivli doctor hiring continues for 1-2 years.
Debt build-up for the capex cycle; management says internal accruals should suffice for several years.
summary.management_tone: Confident on operations and the Dombivli ramp-up, but deliberately conservative on guidance ("I don't want to give you a very aggressive guidance"). Evasive on the exact debt and cash figures ("roughly INR500 crores") and on unit-level profit modelling.
key_quotes: So operational EBITDA drag or losses are only anticipated in the initial 1 or 2 years of operations.
Currently, I don't think we want to be very adventurous and aggressive in guidance.

adds.what: Dombivli Hospital ~300 more beds to be commissioned (on top of ~200 operating)
Three upcoming projects, line of sight to ~3,000 beds in total over five years
Indore next phase of expansion being readied

growth.why: No numeric FY27 revenue guidance; management held Dombivli EBITDA loss guidance at INR2-3 crores per month with breakeven in 1.5-2 years, and the ~300-bed Dombivli addition and ~3,000-bed five-year pipeline are named but without capex or dated orders, so backing is partial.
